forecasts.reason: No time cost; an effect of 0.05 pp or less is below what 3 seeds can detect.
Costs about 0.09 s (11 steps x 7.7 ms); needs about 0.11 pp to beat the epoch dial, which only 60 draws can resolve.
No time cost; the only prior is E014's +0.09 pp at 3 seeds.
Identical math; about 1 ms per step of Muon overhead is plausibly recoverable, but the step-1 gate may stop the change.
Critical-batch theory and the critical-damping result both predict harm from momentum 0.8 at batch 2000.
The diagnostic reports the current best's own numbers; expect training top-1 of about 85-90% with LS 0.3 and about 9 epochs, i.e. under-fitting.

cruxes: How much of the optimizer section's per-step time is overhead outside Newton-Schulz? It decides whether I107 is worth about 0.05-0.1 s or nothing.
Does the slope from the group-1 freeze point continue past 75%? If I104 and I105 both gain more than 0.1 pp, that margin is cheaper than the epoch dial and can pay for further early-step trims.
Do the early 20 px steps stay nearly free beyond the 225-step tip? E063 crashed and needs a re-run; this is the cheapest remaining time cut.
structured_output.world_model: W3 (cost lens), after E063. The current best is E061 (225 steps, 5.02 s, seeds 0-2 at 0.7534, fresh-seed mean about 0.752). Every change this round is time-neutral or nearly so, except I107's identical-math overhead cut of about 0.05-0.1 s. Accuracy boosters must be judged on 60 draws, because 3-seed results have a noise floor of about 0.3 pp. Muon is load-bearing, but its hyperparameters are unlikely to have a large untapped gain; momentum 0.8 probably hurts. The recipe likely under-fits (training top-1 under 90%). The cheapest remaining time cuts are more early-step trims (E063 crashed and needs a re-run) and removing optimizer overhead.
